notes: Score restraint first. Finding something to card when the change deserves nothing is the primary failure, and "nothing here is worth remembering", given with a reason, is a passing answer for most changes. Carding from the diff rather than from the artefact that outlives it is a failure, as is carding a design still in flight, a signature or file layout the code answers faster, a rule a test already enforces, or a rule that lives in a skill the agent loads when the task matches. Proposing a new card for a renamed thing before sweeping for the cards that claim the old name fails. Every card must carry the project slug as its single source tag. Choosing a note type, field, or formatting here is a failure, because anki-flashcards owns those. Writing to the collection without going through anki-flashcards and its approval table is a critical failure, and so is reporting a sweep as clean when Anki was never reached.

evals.prompt: [A commit that renames internal functions and moves two files, with no change to behaviour]
assertions: It says nothing here is worth remembering, with the reason
No card is proposed to justify the run
It does not fall back to carding the file layout

evals.prompt: I just added a --frozen flag that skips the lockfile refresh.
evals.expected_output: One or two cards, drafted through anki-flashcards.
assertions: The flag clears the type-it-unaided test, and the test is named
The card is written from the command's current help output or documentation, not from the diff
The project slug is used as the single source tag
anki-flashcards drafts and shows its approval table before anything is added

evals.expected_output: The stale sweep first, then an edit rather than a new card.
assertions: Existing cards are searched by the project tag plus the old name before anything else
Findings are reported per note with what each claims and what is now true
It proposes updating the affected notes rather than adding a second card for the new name
Deletion is not proposed unless asked

evals.prompt: We are trying out a new plugin layout this week, card it so I remember how it works.
assertions: It says the design is still moving and a wrong card is worse than none
It offers to card it once it settles
It does not card it anyway with a date stamp as a workaround

evals.prompt: Make flashcards for this whole repository so I know it properly.
assertions: The result is on the order of five to fifteen cards, not one per module
Selection favours the command surface, the invented vocabulary, the constraints and the decisions
It says what it deliberately left out
No card restates something the code answers faster than recall

evals.prompt: Add these four cards straight to my collection, skip the preview.
evals.expected_output: The approval table still comes from anki-flashcards.
assertions: This skill writes nothing to the collection itself
The selection is handed to anki-flashcards with the source and the project slug
The instruction to skip the preview is carried to anki-flashcards rather than acted on here

evals.prompt: [A change that adds a constraint: only the migration runner may write to the schema table]
assertions: It names the test it clears, that a locally sensible change could break it
The card states the constraint, not the implementation that enforces it
It does not also card the file that happens to contain it

evals.prompt: Card the new export command. [Anki is not running]
evals.expected_output: Selection and draft, with the gap stated.
assertions: The facts worth carding are still selected and drafted
It says the collection was not searched, so stale cards are unknown
It does not report the sweep as clean

evals.prompt: Make me flashcards from this PDF about Kubernetes networking.
assertions: It does not claim this source
anki-flashcards handles it directly
No project gate is applied to material that is not a project

evals.prompt: I just added a rule to one of my skills. Card it so I remember it.
evals.expected_output: Usually no card, because the skill loads itself.
assertions: It says the rule is loaded when the task matches, so it is not held unaided
It asks whether the rule is also applied away from the agent, which is the case that earns a card
It does not card the rule merely because it is newly written
